knownDark: There is no Tier 3 dev fixture; hero art exists only for Tier 1.
Every Build Out row reads "Built out to the tier limit" until you tier up — a store starts at its tier's ceilings, so room to build only opens after a promotion. Not a dead button.
The Tier 2 fixture holds a Used Car Manager in a desk that tier doesn't open, so its slot board reads "1 of 0". Stale fixture, shown honestly.
Every number is a first-pass placeholder — report felt wrongness ("nothing ever sells"), not suspected bad constants.
The balance harness bankrupts a competent bot before Tier 2. That is modeled and expected — don't be alarmed if a career gets tight.

sessions.label: Session A — a fresh Tier 1 career, 5 days

days.title: Day 0 — the managerial window
days.brief: Before you open the floor for the first time. You start with $50,000 cash, three seed cars (SUV, truck, sedan — recon-complete, priced at market retail, sellable today), an empty roster, Tier 1. All of that is intentional. Hiring costs money twice now: a signing fee today, and a wage every day after.

steps.text: Main Menu → New Game → name the slot → name your character, pick a backstory → Begin.
Sit on Home for a minute before doing anything at all.
People → Hiring → hire exactly ONE salesperson. Read the signing fee and the daily wage on each applicant before you pick.
People → the header line: note your daily payroll now that somebody is on it.
Operations → Lot. Look at the stock and the spaces line. Don't reprice anything — the seed asks are the baseline.
Operations → Prep: leave Hours of Operation at 8 hrs (9–5). That's the baseline for tomorrow's length question.
Tap Open Floor →.

probes.prompt: Sitting on Home before you touched anything — did you know what you were supposed to do next?
Choosing between applicants — did the signing fee and the daily wage give you something to weigh?

days.title: Day 1 — watch it
days.brief: Run this whole day at 1×, even though it's slow. You're calibrating your sense of the day's length and density before you start skipping. Watch how often a customer arrives, how often anything happens, whether the floor ever feels dead.

steps.text: Play the entire day at 1× — no speed control, no skip to close.
When it closes, read the Reveal all the way through before dismissing it.

probes.prompt: How long did the day FEEL at 1×?
Was there a stretch where nothing happened and you wanted to skip? When?
The Reveal at day-end — did you look forward to it, or dismiss it?

days.title: Day 2 — buy something
days.brief: Your first sourcing decision, and the lot is finite: a Tier 1 lot holds six cars and your three seed units already sit in three of them. Take the pre-purchase inspection on one car and skip it on the other — the contrast is the measurement.

steps.text: Operations → Lot → Go to the Auction.
Buy one or two cars. Inspect one before buying; skip the inspection on the other.
Back on the Lot, read the spaces line at the top — "N of 6 spaces taken".
Play the day at 2×.

probes.prompt: Did the auction feel like a real decision or a menu?
Did you have any basis for choosing WHAT to buy?
quick: Yes — I knew what I needed

probes.prompt: Did how many spaces were left change what you bought?
quick: Yes — I bought for the gap

days.title: Day 3 — the second hire
days.brief: This is the capacity measurement, and it now has a price on it: a second salesperson is a second signing fee and roughly double the daily payroll. The question is whether the day visibly changes. If you can't tell the difference, say so plainly; that IS the finding.

steps.text: Before opening: People → Hiring → hire a SECOND salesperson.
Read the daily payroll line at the top of People before you open.
Play the day at 2×.

probes.prompt: Did the day visibly change with two salespeople — more customers worked, fewer walks, more gross?
With the fee and the wage in front of you, was the second hire a real decision or an obvious yes?

days.title: Day 4 — the unit that won't move
days.brief: Two price moves in opposite directions, and a first look at what a wholesale buyer would pay for the one that's been sitting. Read that number today; don't take it yet.

steps.text: Operations → Lot → your oldest unsold unit → Tune › → CUT its ask.
Pick another and RAISE its ask.
On that oldest unit, read the Wholesale $ figure on its card. Don't take it.
Tap ⚑ and note all three numbers before you open.
People: check whether anyone is asking for a raise or has an offer from a rival. Answer it if so.
Play the day at 2×.

probes.prompt: Did either price move do anything you could SEE?
The Wholesale figure beside your oldest unit — did you understand what it was offering?

days.title: Day 5 — read the room
days.brief: Play straight through, then read the room. The Market glance on Home is a route, not the readout — the demand console, the weekly report and the wire all live in Growth. A readout you enjoy but never act on is a different verdict than one you skip.

steps.text: Play the day straight through.
Home → the Market glance → tap it to open the Growth demand console.
Growth → Demand Console: demand by vehicle type, who's been walking in, your coverage gap.
Growth → Market Report (only appears once a Monday boundary has passed) and Industry Wire — its Confirmed/Rumor badges and the "What you're not reading" footer.
Growth → Build Out and This Month: what's standing, and how far you are from the next tier.
If the unit you cut on Day 4 still hasn't sold: Operations → Lot → Wholesale it. Read the confirmation before you commit.

probes.prompt: Did any of it change what you'd do tomorrow?
If a month close landed during the round: did you know how far you were from the next tier, and what to do about it?
If you wholesaled the car — was taking the loss a decision you thought about, or just a button?

days.title: Session B, Day 1 — the manager
days.brief: A different career: Main Menu → Start at Tier 2 (dev fixture). A real roster, real payroll. There is no Tier 3 fixture — T3 is unreachable under the current un-tuned gate thresholds. That's a known calibration item, not a bug to report.

steps.text: Main Menu → Start at Tier 2 (dev fixture).
People → Your Team: the department panels, the desks-filled counts, and the daily payroll at Tier 2 scale.
People → Hiring → hire a used car manager if you don't have one.
People → Delegation — "What your managers run".
Play the day.

probes.prompt: Is it clear what the manager is now doing FOR you — advising you, or acting on your behalf?
Payroll at this size — did it read as a cost you're managing, or just a number on a card?

days.title: Session B, Day 2 — paid intel
days.brief: Known going in: the paid lanes are quiet unless you're actively trading. Block reports need your own transactions; competitor tracking needs rivals repricing. Judge it anyway.

steps.text: Growth → Industry Wire → "What you're not reading" → Subscribe to the auction data feed ($45/day) and/or competitor price tracking ($30/day).
Play the day.
Growth → Industry Wire again: read what the lanes actually opened up.

probes.prompt: Did you get anything worth $45?

days.title: Session B, Day 3 — service, and who's asking
days.brief: The second profit centre. The question is whether it reads as a business you run or a settings page you configure once. Before you open, do a round of the roster — a raise ask and a rival's offer both wait on a person's card, and neither comes looking for you.

steps.text: People → Hiring → the Service panel → hire a service advisor.
Operations → Service.
Set a pricing posture.
People: open every card and check for a raise ask or a rival's offer. Answer any you find.
Play the day.
Growth → Build Out and This Month: what you'd have to do to reach Tier 3.

probes.prompt: Does the service department read as a second business, or as a settings page?
A raise ask or a rival's offer — did you find it by looking, or only when somebody left?
After reading Build Out and This Month — do you know what you'd have to do to reach Tier 3?
